based_on: The site is at the southwest corner of College Street and Henry Street, covering about 1,617 square metres.
The application proposes to increase the approved building height from 31 storeys to 45 storeys.
The proposal increases the total number of residential units from 490 to 684, which includes 545 affordable rental units.
The proposal adds 137 affordable two-bedroom rental units, which would have affordable rents for 40 years.
The 137 additional affordable units may qualify for financial incentives from the City, such as waived fees and charges.
The development will continue to provide 12 replacement rental dwelling rooms, and eligible tenants would keep the right to return at similar rents.
The designated heritage properties on the site are to be kept and built into the new development.
The proposal includes 6 vehicle parking spaces at ground level.
A total of 695 bicycle parking spaces are proposed for the building.
An Official Plan Amendment is needed to change Site and Area Specific Policy 533 to allow the new building height.
A Zoning By-law Amendment is needed to change Exception CR 1010 to allow the increased density, height, massing, and other standards.
Staff recommend that City Council amend the Official Plan for 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street.
Staff recommend that City Council amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the site.
Staff recommend that City Council allow the City Solicitor to update or replace existing agreements for dwelling room replacement and affordable housing.
Staff recommend putting a holding provision on the Zoning By-law until the Functional Servicing and Stormwater Management Report is revised, reviewed, and accepted.
The owner must pay cash-in-lieu for parkland dedication before the first above-ground building permit is issued.
